biography.plain_text: Tim Armand is an American digital-media entrepreneur who co-founded Health Union with Olivier Chateau after a senior marketing career at GlaxoSmithKline. Their Philadelphia-based company developed online communities for people with chronic conditions and attracted private-equity backing. Armand served as founding president before moving to its board, retaining a role in the business he helped build.

long_biography.plain_text:
At Health Union, Tim Armand helped establish a network of condition-specific websites that gave people with chronic illness a place to exchange experience. Migraine.com was the first. The company kept patient content separate from clearly labelled advertising, while also offering research and clinical-trial services to healthcare partners. Armand's earlier work in pharmaceutical eBusiness informed the digital approach.

Armand and Olivier Chateau began the venture in a small office, doing much of the early work themselves. As founding president, Armand handled corporate and financial responsibilities while the network widened beyond its original condition. He handed those executive duties to a new leadership team in 2021 and remained a voting director and adviser to Chateau.
